test_title: PYST 73: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 30 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following examples represents motion along a straight line?

options.text: A child running around a park
A train moving on a straight track

solution:
The correct answer is __**A train moving on a straight track**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Motion** is defined as the change in the **position** of an object with respect to **time** and its surrounding environment. Depending on the path taken by the object, motion is classified into various types.
 
• **Rectilinear Motion**: This refers to the movement of an object along a **straight line**. In this type of motion, the **direction** of the object remains constant throughout its path.
 
• **A fan blade rotating**: This represents **rotational motion** or **circular motion**. The particles of the fan blades move in a circular path around a **fixed axis**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **A child running around a park**: Since a park usually involves a curved or circular boundary, the path is not a single straight line. This is typically an example of **curvilinear motion** or **circular motion**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **A train moving on a straight track**: When a train travels on tracks that do not curve, every part of the train moves the same distance in a **straight path**. This is a classic example of **rectilinear motion**. *Hence, this option is correct.*
 
• **A pendulum swinging**: This is an example of **periodic motion** or **oscillatory motion**. The bob of the pendulum moves **to and fro** about a central **mean position** at regular intervals of **time**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Translatory Motion**:
 
 
• It occurs when all parts of an object move the **same distance** in the same **interval of time**.
 
• It is divided into two categories: **Rectilinear motion** (motion in a **straight line**, e.g., a **falling stone**) and **Curvilinear motion** (motion along a **curved path**, e.g., a **thrown ball**).
 
 
 
• **Circular and Rotational Motion**:
 
 
• **Circular motion** is when an object moves along the **circumference** of a circle (e.g., a **satellite** orbiting the **Earth**).
 
• **Rotational motion** occurs when an object turns around an **internal axis** (e.g., the **spinning of the Earth** or a **spinning top**).
 
 
 
• **Periodic and Oscillatory Motion**:
 
 
• **Periodic motion** repeats itself after a fixed **period of time** (e.g., **hands of a clock**).
 
• **Oscillatory motion** is a specific type of periodic motion where the object moves **back and forth** (e.g., **vibrating strings** of a **guitar** or a **child on a swing**).
 
 
 
• **Random Motion**:
 
 
• This occurs when an object moves in a **disorderly manner** with no fixed path or direction (e.g., the **motion of a honeybee** or **gas molecules**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Distance vs. Displacement**: In **rectilinear motion**, if an object moves in a single direction without turning back, the magnitude of **distance** is equal to the magnitude of **displacement**.
 
• **Uniform Rectilinear Motion**: When an object covers **equal distances** in **equal intervals of time** along a straight line, it is said to be in **uniform motion**, meaning its **velocity** is constant.
 
• **Non-Uniform Rectilinear Motion**: If the **speed** of the object changes while moving in a straight line, it is called **accelerated motion** or non-uniform linear motion (e.g., a **car** starting from rest on a straight road).
 
• **Newton's First Law**: It states that an object will remain in its state of **rest** or **uniform motion** in a **straight line** unless acted upon by an **external unbalanced force**.
